components.css: .ds-ticket { position:relative; display:flex; min-height:300px; padding:3rem; flex-direction:column; justify-content:center; color:var(--paper,#f4f1e8); background:var(--ink,#173e32); font-family:'DM Mono',ui-monospace,monospace; transform:rotate(1.5deg); box-shadow:14px 18px 38px rgba(23,62,50,.18); } .ds-ticket::before { position:absolute; inset:-7px 0 auto; height:14px; background:var(--paper,#f4f1e8); content:''; clip-path:polygon(0 50%,5% 0,10% 50%,15% 0,20% 50%,25% 0,30% 50%,35% 0,40% 50%,45% 0,50% 50%,55% 0,60% 50%,65% 0,70% 50%,75% 0,80% 50%,85% 0,90% 50%,95% 0,100% 50%,100% 100%,0 100%); } .ds-ticket span { max-width:28ch; line-height:1.6; } .ds-ticket strong { margin:1.75rem 0 .3rem; color:var(--lime,#dff29a); font-family:'Fraunces',Georgia,serif; font-size:4.2rem; font-variant-numeric:tabular-nums; line-height:.9; letter-spacing:-.03em; } .ds-ticket small { opacity:.75; }

narrative.overview:
The system treats a satirical calculator as a refined café artifact: warm cream paper, dark green ink, considered editorial type, menu rules, and receipt geometry. Its personality comes from the tension between polished hospitality design and sober tabular arithmetic rather than from novelty decoration.

Fraunces supplies generous, high-contrast headlines and oversized numeric moments; DM Mono makes descriptions, labels, inputs, and calculations feel itemized and exact. Slightly rotated ticket surfaces and torn paper edges provide tactile wit, while the surrounding composition stays spacious, direct, and highly legible.
keyCharacteristics: Cream paper and dark green ink establish the default reading surface.
Avocado and lime accents belong on dark surfaces; orange and orange ink mark high-attention details according to contrast.
Editorial display type and monospaced data type keep emotion and arithmetic in productive tension.
Rules, dashed separators, receipt edges, tabular numerals, and restrained rotation create the café-menu world.
A direct first-viewport jump leads to the live calculator without hiding the satirical premise.

rules.name: The Surface-Aware Citrus Rule
rules.body: Use burnt orange ink on cream paper and brighter citrus orange on dark green; never swap them merely for variety.

rules.name: The Green Field Rule
rules.body: Large dark fields are deep green, not black, and their light text remains warm cream, not pure white.

rules.name: The Editorial-and-Register Rule
rules.body: Fraunces expresses the premise and totals; DM Mono explains, labels, and records the calculation.

rules.name: The Numeric Alignment Rule
rules.body: Changing prices, years, and currency totals use tabular numerals wherever the implementation presents them as comparable data.

rules.name: The Shared Edge Rule
rules.body: Full-bleed sections may change the field color, but their content edges must return to the same centered shell as the rest of the page.

rules.name: The Paper Artifact Rule
rules.body: Elevation belongs to ticket and receipt objects only; ordinary sections and menu items remain flat.

rules.name: The No Generic Card Rule
rules.body: Do not round content into conventional cards; use paper fields, rules, clipping, and restrained rotation when an object needs a boundary.

dos: Do keep cream paper and deep green ink as the dominant field relationship.
Do reserve avocado and lime for dark surfaces and choose the orange token appropriate to the surface beneath it.
Do pair Fraunces editorial statements with DM Mono labels, explanations, and live data.
Do use rules, torn edges, tabular figures, and slight rotation to sustain the café-menu and receipt metaphor.
Do preserve visible focus, real labels, live result announcements, and reduced-motion behavior.
Do collapse all paired desktop grids to a clear single-column reading order at 760px and below.
donts: Don't introduce generic rounded cards, soft dashboard panels, or a broad radius scale.
Don't use pure black, pure white, or unrelated saturated accents in place of the established botanical and paper palette.
Don't add shadows to ordinary content sections or animate decorative objects without an interaction purpose.
Don't turn numeric inputs into decorative readouts; they must remain directly editable and keyboard accessible.
Don't strand the calculator below introductory content without the first-viewport jump link.
